description: Indeterminate form (∞-∞ or ∞*0) at infinity involving logarithms: reduce to the standard limit ln(1+X)/X -> 0 as X->0.

exercises.technique: ∞-∞ (log difference) at infinity. Combine logs: ln(x+2)-ln x = ln(1+2/x) → 0 as x→∞ (standard log limit form), and 2/(x+2) → 0, leaving only the constant 1/4.
∞-∞ growth-rate comparison. Factor out x: x(2-7/x-11 ln x/x). As x→∞, ln x/x → 0, so the bracket → 2, and x·2 → +∞; linear growth always beats logarithmic growth.
∞·0 at infinity, reduced directly with the given standard log limit by substituting X=1/x → 0, turning x·ln(1+1/x) into ln(1+X)/X.
